_theMergedRung: ⛔ `regional` IS RETIRED INTO `heroic`, AND HEROIC KEEPS ITS OWN FLOOR OF 25 — nobody moves. ⚠️ I first set it to 12, reasoning that 25 would strand levels 6–24; THAT WAS WRONG and the suite caught it in one run. A rung's top is defined by the NEXT rung's floor, so retiring `regional` simply widens `notable` to 5–24. ⛑ The merged rung holds 70 people and is the fattest on the ladder, which is right for the rung most of a campaign is spent at.
_mythicIsItsOwnBand: ⛑ ERIK, RULED: 'must add mythic'. It sits on 5 authored NPCs, appeared in neither of the old label sets, and was the loose end in every previous draft. One rung per tier means it simply has a home — no rename, no sharing, nothing banded under a word that was not meant for it.
_oneVocabulary: ⚠️ THERE IS NO SEPARATE PLAYER LADDER. novice/adept/master/heroic/legendary is retired: a character and an opponent are described by the same six words, and a level-30 player and a level-30 foe are both `heroic`. ⛑ The engine reasons in `band`; the tier name is what a person is called.
_whyMoreRungsIsNotAProblem: ⛑ ERIK ASKED. MEASURED BEFORE ANSWERING: every rung is populated — riffraff 6 · notable 15 · heroic 70 · epic 31 · legendary 18 · mythic 5 — so no band is starved and none has to borrow. ⚠️ AND MORE RUNGS MAKES THE ONE FILTER THAT MATTERS SHARPER: the '+1 glimpse of the legendary' is a one-rung reach, and a one-rung reach on a six-rung ladder is a real constraint where on a four-rung one it was nearly the whole roster. ⛔ THE COST IS A LONGER LIST IN A UI AND NOTHING ELSE. The bands are not evenly wide on purpose — 1–4 then 5–11 then 12–39 — because early levels pass quickly and late ones do not.

_subAttributeDistribution_20260917: ⛔ MEASURED 2026-09-17, PER VERB-SLOT — THE WAY IT ACTUALLY ROLLS, not per craft. `stampCraftSubAttributes` stamps EVERY function, and 164 of 432 crafts roll more than one sub, so a per-craft count is the wrong unit and I used it twice before getting this right. Across 1048 verb-slots: **reason 219 (20.9%) · insight 196 (18.7%) · craft 150 (14.3%) · rapport 140 (13.4%) · wits 130 (12.4%) · presence 90 (8.6%) · strength 64 (6.1%) · agility 59 (5.6%).** ⚠️ SO THE MENTAL ATTRIBUTE CARRIES 415 OF 1048 SLOTS — 40% — AND PHYSICAL CARRIES 123, WHICH IS 12%. A 3.4:1 imbalance between attributes, and it is not a misclassification: it is what the corpus is. This is a game about knowing things. ⛔ AND IT NOW HAS A DIRECT CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING. The eight nexuses each amplify one sub-attribute at +6. **Whoever holds Arcology Crown (reason) amplifies 219 verb-slots; whoever holds Plexus Solaris (agility) amplifies 59.** A nexus is worth 3.7× another purely by which faculty it happens to hold, before anybody fights over one. ⬜ ERIK'S CALL, AND THERE ARE THREE ANSWERS. (1) LEAVE IT — the imbalance is honest and a reason-nexus SHOULD be the prize. (2) INVERT THE MAGNITUDE so a rare-faculty nexus is worth proportionally more, which makes all eight equally contested and is a one-line table. (3) RE-ATTRIBUTE some mental crafts, which is months of work and would fight the corpus. ⛑ **I would take (2).** The organs were mapped to what each site already was, not to balance — so fixing it at the magnitude rather than the mapping keeps the meaning and fixes the maths.
_subAttributePassComplete_20260917: ⛑ AND THE MISCLASSIFICATION PASS IS DONE: no craft remains that matches the documented §166 defect shape. 27 carry an authored `subAttribute` and 17 carry a LEFT: verdict with a reason. ⚠️ I ran three wrong measurements on the way here and each was caught by the next one: I counted per-craft instead of per-verb; I asserted presence was 'starved at 28' when it is 57 crafts and 90 slots; and I theorised that presence was harm-gated when 20 of its 27 authored crafts carry no harm verb at all. ⛔ THE DEFAULT IS POWER, NOT FINESSE — a social craft rolls `presence` unless its verb is on the finesse list, which is the opposite of what I claimed before reading `craftSubAttribute`.
